thesis: Historical and contemporary cases expose different mechanisms rather than civilizational personalities.
role: Compare deliberation, organized violence, kinship, culture and demography across numbered chapters 8A–18 opening.

ideas.statement: Internal cooperation can coexist with organized external violence.
Genetic signals often underdetermine historical social causes.
Rice cooperation changes measured culture rapidly; endogamy alters genomic structure over generations.
Cultural influence, population replacement and genetic trait selection are not interchangeable.
Religious fertility depends on retention and institutions, not violent extremism.
Urban housing, work timing and care costs can constrain family formation without explicit prohibition.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A peaceful segmentary-lineage model can also produce a Y-chromosome bottleneck.
Chichén Itzá ritual victims and long-term regional continuity can coexist.
Political-extreme pooled association is small and inconsistent by country.
Childlessness may signal prestigious autonomy in one setting, large families status in another.
The agricultural cooperation mechanism connects production and learned psychology.
South Asian contrast concerns persistent endogamy rather than rapid learned behavior.
Digital dating filters can produce assortative mating and ideological isolation within cosmopolitan cities.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Self-domestication mechanism disputed; war does not establish a conqueror gene.
Endogamy says nothing simple about superiority or personality.
Good-enough caution must not become pronatalist coercion.
Political labels differ across societies; no inevitable extremist inheritance.
Migration and contextual costs must be disentangled.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
